referents.why: third plural 'they' handed Jesus over; the chief priests (w4, masculine plural) are the agent carried through the verse, the first-named subject
referents.category: implied subject of a finite verb

links.why: participle having formed a counsel is nested in the main act of the chief priests
participle having bound Jesus is nested in the main act of leading him away
Greek kai is a separate word, not fused into the verb, so the link is and, not and then
second finite act of the same agent (handed over) joined by separate kai

groups.why: two finite acts of the chief priests (led away, handed over), each stating its subject only in the verb; recorded as a reading for review

none_fit.what: anterior participles (having formed a counsel, having bound Jesus) that precede the main act; no link type for prior circumstance, so kept as within

cant_tell.what: referent of cl3s (they, who handed Jesus over)
cant_tell.why: the subject is the chief priests together with elders, scribes and the Council; no candidate covers them together (c8 is elders and scribes only), so w4 is chosen as the first-named agent
